content: To add a per-request dimension (tenant/user/trace) to dozens of storage functions without editing every signature and call site, read it from an AsyncLocalStorage store inside the lowest-level resolver (e.g. getPaths). Absent a scope, fall back to the legacy default so local/stdio/tests stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Background work decoupled from the request must carry the dimension EXPLICITLY and re-enter the scope — a per-user queue is the natural explicit boundary.
context: T-044 (ADR-005 decision 1). Chose ALS over adding a userId param to ~50 storage fns; getPaths() reads the scope, http.ts wraps each /mcp + /sync request in runWithTenant, and synthesis-queue.ts carries userId explicitly + re-enters runWithTenant in its worker. Result: engines unchanged, all 179 prior tests passed unmodified. Reviewer verified ALS propagates through the MCP SDK's synchronous onmessage dispatch inside awaited handleRequest.
title: Use AsyncLocalStorage to thread a request-scoped dimension through many functions
